episodes.194513: As the remains of Tropical System Francine slowly meandered through the mid South, a persistent band of showers and thunderstorms produced very heavy rainfall totals over the two day period from the 13th into the 14th.  Some of the heaviest rains occurred during the evening of the 13th into the morning hours of the 14th in parts of northwest and north central Alabama. Widespread rain totals of 2 to 4 inches were observed, with a large pocket of 4 to 6 inch rainfall across portions of Cullman, Colbert, Franklin, Lauderdale, Lawrence, and Morgan.  A smaller pocket of 8 to 12 inch rainfall was observed in Lawrence Cunty, including the Bankhead National Forest.  During the evening hours of the 13th, a few instances of flash flooding weres reported in Cullman County. During the late night and morning hours of the 14th, significant flash and areal flooding occurred as a result in the town of Moulton and nearby areas where several homes were affected by flood water.  Small stream and creek flooding persisted through the 15th as runoff fed into the Big Nance Creek which went into Major Flood during the morning hours.  A man was rescued from flood waters during the early morning hours of the 15th just south of Courtland near a creek feeding into Big Nance Creek.
episodes.194572: Increased monsoonal moisture from the remnants of Tropical Storm Ileana moved northward from the Gulf of California into New Mexico on September 15th. Scattered virga showers and thunderstorms developed over portions of northern and central NM. One produced a rogue gust of 63 mph at the Raton Municipal Airport.
episodes.194597: Hurricane Francine made landfall along the Louisiana coast during the afternoon of September 11. Downgraded to a tropical depression as it moved northward through Mississippi the next day, Francine brought gradient wind gusts of 30-40 mph to Central Alabama. Numerous trees were downed across several counties, with some falling on power lines and across roadways. One minor injury occurred in Jefferson County when a tree fell onto a passing pickup truck.||The next couple days brought bands of heavy rainfall and gusty winds to the area as activity became increasing associated with a nearly stationary surface boundary. One storm in Blount County on the 13th produced hail over quarter-size, with another storm shortly after causing an area of tree and minor structural damage near Locust Fork. Heavy rainfall caused flooding issues in Birmingham the morning of the 14th, in Eufaula around midday on the 14th, and in Birmingham again just after midnight on the 15th.
episodes.194606: A line of strong thunderstorms developed along the Laramie Range in southeast Wyoming during the afternoon of September 15th. Segments of this line moved east into the high plains along and east of Interstate 25, and produced mainly quarter sized hail and isolated wind gusts over 60 MPH.
episodes.194609: A strong/severe thunderstorm tracked north across Weld County and produced 1.5 inch hail south of Kersey.
episodes.194627: Several showers and thunderstorms developed in association with the remnants of Hurricane Francine and a stalled frontal boundary.  Several areas of rotation were detected, but no tornado touchdowns were reported.  There was one report of a tree down in Walton county.  In addition, heavy rainfall led to areas of flash flooding.
episodes.194636: Several showers and thunderstorms developed in association with the remnants of Hurricane Francine and a stalled frontal boundary.  Several areas of rotation were detected, but no tornado touchdowns were reported.  There was one report of a tree down in Walton county.  In addition, heavy rainfall led to areas of flash flooding.
episodes.194947: A strong to severe thunderstorm moved north across Weston County, producing wind gusts to around 60 mph across the area.
episodes.195275: A strong trough digging into the Great Basin gradually shifted through the region, resulting in multiple days of scattered thunderstorm development and associated severe wind gusts.
episodes.195561: Thunderstorms developed across NW Kansas and NE Colorado during the afternoon and trekked into SW Nebraska. These storms produced penny size hail to the north of Benkelman.
episodes.195961: Potential Tropical Cyclone #8 located off the SC coast was classified by the National Hurricane Center on September 15 and a Tropical Storm Warning was issued for the entire coast of southeast NC and northeast SC at that time. The system slowly moved toward the coast but never became organized enough to be classified as a tropical (or subtropical) cyclone, eventually moving inland around the NC/SC border on September 16. The system brought historic rainfall amounts and extensive flash flooding to portions of southeast North Carolina, focused most in Carolina Beach  where 29 adults, 2 children, 5 dogs, and 3 cats required water rescue from the local Fire Departments. In addition, tropical storm force gusts, minor to moderate coastal flooding, and 1 tornado occurred.
episodes.196056: Thunderstorms developed along a stationary front, situated over western Nebraska during the afternoon and evening hours of September 14th. Two areas of storms developed, the first over Lincoln county and a second area over the northwestern Sandhills. Ping pong ball sized hail was reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.196251: A weak stationary frontal boundary combined with a weak upper-level disturbance and remnant atmospheric moisture from former Tropical Storm Ileana (central Gulf of California) to provide slow moving mid to late afternoon thunderstorms from Harlingen to  Brownsville. Between 3.5 and just under 6 inches fell, with rainfall rates nearing 3 inches per hour for up to two hours in areas from central Brownsville to east Harlingen where flooding was reported.
episodes.196353: Heavy rainfall led to flash flooding, with water in homes, in Edgewater.
episodes.196468: An upper level trough over California heads east over Nevada along with moisture which enhanced atmospheric instability, creating periods of strong thunderstorms over northern and central Nevada.
episodes.196475: Convergent and moist light southerly flow over South Florida supported the development of scattered showers across the Gulf waters on the morning of Septermber 15th.
episodes.196621: Several severe thunderstorm wind gusts recorded on the 15th.
episodes.196730: A line of high based showers and thunderstorms moved off of the Wind River Range and brought high wind to portions of central Wyoming. Wind gusts over 58 mph were reported from Lander to west of Riverton. Some notable wind gusts included 71 mph at the Lander Airport and 68 mph to the west of Riverton.
episodes.196773: Isolated thunderstorms moved across Southeastern Arizona causing uprooted trees in SE Tucson area and in the Benson area.
episodes.196857: Ridge like flow allowed for high based storms to develop and for them to produce strong winds.
episodes.196868: A waterspout was observed north of Bahia Honda Key in association with a thunderstorms. The environment featured an atmosphere with deep moisture and very little convective inhibition.  A stationary front was located to the north over the Florida peninsula.
episodes.196891: A very strong thunderstorm peaked in intensity as it crossed from Mexico into the Laredo area on the night of September 14th. This initial storm contained heavy rain rates and weas then followed by a few other storms in wake during the early morning hours of the 15th. This combination and the flash prone urban area lead to quick flooding on streets and water rescues. Frequent lightning impacted power lines and caused power outages across the city.
episodes.196985: In a typical summertime pattern, convection fired up along the seabreeze during the afternoon timeframe. One cell was able to take advantage of vorticiy from surrounding boundaries and produced a brief waterspout along the Mississippi coast.
episodes.196989: Heavy rain brought flooding to the Cache River at Patterson from middle to late September.

events.narrative: Flash flooding was reported across Headland with road closures and over 9 inches of rain in a 5 hour period.
The public reported that County Road 22 was underwater.

TV station KGNS stated that law enforcement in Laredo reported several streets flooded and water rescues across the city. A total of 9 children and adults were rescued from their vehicle in flooded waters. Moderate to heavy rain was falling from 10 PM CST to 5 AM CST with flooded streets persisting through the rest of the morning.

Lightning struck the 1600 block of Jacaman Rd, that resulted in a fire. Multiple power lines were reported down. There were temporary power outages across the city, with over 2,000 people without electricity through the morning hours on the 15th.
The public reported flooding in the Pansey area due to heavy rain in a short period of time.
Flooding in the Malone area resulted in a sewer backup.

Multiple water rescues in vehicles occurred overnight in Birmingham following heavy rainfall that led to flash flooding. Several roadways in neighborhoods on the west side of downtown Birmingham were flooded, resulting in several calls concerning vehicles stranded in water. Interstate 59/20 was briefly flooded near Arkadelphia Rd. Village Creek and Valley Creek also quickly rose into Flood Stage between midnight and 2 am. A couple reports were received on the east side of downtown near the airport as well, notably along Appalachee St and Messer Airport Highway.
The public reported that Boynton Street was closed due to flooding.
A man was rescued from flood waters at the intersection of CR 150 and CR 257. This is near a small creek that feeds into nearby Big Nance Creek. Depth of water estimated at 2-3 feet.
There was a report of water entering a residence off Highway 2 in the Bascom area.
A photo on social media showed water up to the porch of a residence in the Malone area.
A few streets remained flooded through the morning hours across the city of Laredo.
The CoCoRaHS station FL-VL-1 in New Smyrna Beach measured 4.74 inches of rainfall.
Station (CRSN2) Crane Springs, Elevation 6414 ft.

events.narrative: A narrow, rope-like waterspout was observed about 2 miles north of Bahia Honda Key.  The condensation cloud extended all the way to the water surface.  Video obtained later from a public observer verified a robust spray ring was attendant to the waterspout.

Harlingen PD received numerous reports of flooded roads during the mid to late afternoon.  These included:  Fair Park Blvd, the intersection of 7th and M St, Spur 5             and Frontage, Eye St, intersection of J St and Fair Park Blvd, Bowie Ave and 25th St,             Frontage Rd. at Primera Rd exit to Wilson Rd, Le Moyne Garden, and Emerald Lake Dr. Texas Department of Transportation was notified and road closures began during the event, with water reported halfway up cars in some spots.

A pocket of torrential rainfall from a nearly stationary isolated thunderstorm, with measured and estimated rainfall between 3 and 4 inches in a very small area around downtown Edinburg, left 3 feet of water in roads around the Courthouse building, some of which entered structures of estimated depths of 1 to 1.5 feet.  Damage was unknown at the time of this writing.
Uprooted tree at the Loves Truck Stop at the intersection of Interstate 10 and Highway 90 found on social media.

San Benito PD reported various levels of flooding across town.  The following reports were received:  One foot of flowing water down Brooks Avenue at around 445 PM CDT; additional flooding on Franklin Road, Woodford Street, and Bowie Street.  Water reportedly entered homes on Bowie Street with one rescue required; water was reportedly at least knee deep in some locations (2 to 3 feet).

Torrential rainfall, as much as 5.48 inches of rain having fallen in 90 minutes in Rancho Viejo, left pockets of flash flooding during the late afternoon between San Pedro and Olmito, including Rancho Viejo. Reports of high water into structures and vehicle rescues were reported during and after the peak of the downpour. Vehicle rescues were reported in Olmito and near Rancho Viejo; water was reportedly entering homes on Melva Court in San Pedro, and Burr Oak Loop and Agave avenue just south of IH-169 in east Olmito. ||Damage values estimated based on the reports received. || Damage information was unknown at the time of this writing.

Torrential rain, with measured an estimated totals of 3.5 to more than 5 inches mainly from downtown across the north and west portions of Brownsville, created numerous instances of flooding and flash flooding. Standing water was reported on the intersection of Pablo Kisel Blvd and Morrison Road. Roadway was nearly impassable. Additional reports from Cameron Co. and Brownsville Emergency Management included:  water covering roads at IH-69E Frontage and Alton Gloor, Old Alice/Barnard/Price.  A water rescue was reported downtown on 11th and Elizabeth.  Water levels in harder hit areas were between 2 and 3 feet (standing).||Damage estimates were unknown as of this writing.
